title: Rapid SLI Drill Playbook for Model Rollouts
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a field-ready, compact playbook for rapidly validating Service Level Indicators (SLIs) and trace anchors during model variant rollouts (canary -> ramp -> global). Focus is on fast drilldown steps operators and SREs can use the first 15–60 minutes after a traffic shift. It emphasizes:
- clear SLI selection (sparse, high-signal)
- trace anchor patterns to jump from an SLI alert to offending requests (no full session rebuild required)
- low-cardinality dashboard wireframes for rapid triage
- short checklists for rollback vs mitigation decisions

Why this exists (motivation):
- Rollouts of new model weights, quantization, or runtime changes can cause subtle regressions (increased token latency p95, KV-cache misses, or output-quality regressions that manifest as increased downstream retries). We need a reproducible, minimal drill that surfaces the problem and gives a fast path to mitigation (fallback to previous model, reduce batch-size, increase cache TTL, or pause rollout).

Quick SLI shortlist (minimal set to evaluate within first 15m):
1) Token generation latency p95 (per-route, 99th if traffic low) — measured from request accept to last token emitted. Query: latency_ms.{route}.p95
2) Upstream retry rate (per-route) — percent of requests that triggered a downstream model fallback or retry. Query: retries.count / requests.count
3) KV-cache hit-rate (prefix-level, per-tenant when possible) — warm vs cold is critical to latency. Query: kv_cache.hits / kv_cache.requests
4) Model error-rate (model-returned errors/exceptions) — includes OOMs, invalid logits, or model-side timeouts. Query: model.errors / model.requests
5) User-facing drop/abort rate — requests terminated early or client reconnects.

Acceptance thresholds to watch (examples, tune to product):
- latency_p95 increase > +30% from baseline for >5m -> start investigation
- retries > 1% absolute increase over baseline for 10m -> urgent
- kv_cache_hit_rate drop > 15% -> suspect cold-cache/regression in routing
- model_error_rate > 0.5% absolute -> consider immediate rollback

Trace anchor strategy (fast jump points):
- Always include four short, high-value trace annotations on the request path: request_id, route_id, model_variant, cache_tag. These should be present in every span (or at least root-child).
- For latency SLI: anchor on "model-inference" span and grab attributes: seq_len, kv_hit, batch_size, device_type, kernel-fallback.
- For retries: anchor on "response-handler" span and inspect status_code + retry_reason tag.
- For cache investigations: anchor on "kv-lookup" span and sample 1:50 requests with full context (include user_agent, tenant_id if permitted).

Sampling guidance and retention tradeoffs:
- Canary windows: sample 100% of traces for the first 30 minutes of a canary, then adaptively drop to 5% if no issues.
- High-cardinality fields (user_id, prompt_text) must be redacted or hashed; prefer tenant_id / route bucketing.
- Retain full traces for any request that hits an SLI alert rule within 24 hours; keep light spans for the rest for 7 days.

Minimal dashboard wireframe (panel list and quick queries):
1) Canary Summary strip: current canary % traffic, active model_variant, request_rate (rps), error_rate
2) Latency heatmap: p50/p95/p99 by route over last 60m (small-multiple for top 6 routes)
3) KV-cache panel: hit rate and absolute miss count by cache_tag (last 60m)
4) Trace anchor sampler: list of latest N sampled traces with span durations and anchor tags (button to open trace view)
5) Retry breakdown: retries by reason (OOM, timeout, mismatch) and model_variant
6) Operator quick-actions: visible toggles for rollback, reduce-canary, pause-rollout (buttons link to runbooks/ops playbooks)

Investigation checklist (first 15 minutes):
- Verify alert validity: check lookback windows and confirm not a noisy metric aggregation bug.
- Compare canary to baseline traffic slice (same tenant cohort if possible).
- Jump to recent full traces for slow requests: check model-inference span attributes for batch_size, device_type, kv_hit.
- If kv_cache_hit_rate dropped: check routing logs for cache-tag misassignment or TTL changes.
- If errors increased: inspect model logs for OOMs or quantization fallbacks.
- If retries/spikes only for specific tenants: consider targeted rollback for that tenant rather than full rollback.

Escalation matrix and decision points:
- If latency_p95 increase > +50% AND error_rate > +0.5% within 10m -> immediate rollback (owner: release-engineering).
- If kv_cache_hit_rate drops but latency impact mild -> try increasing cache warm TTL or pinning canary to fewer nodes (owner: serving-runtime).
- If problems isolated to single region -> route canary off that region and continue monitoring (owner: infra/edge).

Playbook snippets (commands and sample queries):
- Fetch recent slow traces (example pseudo-query):
  trace.search("service:model-inference AND duration_ms>300 AND tag:model_variant:canary-v2") order by timestamp desc limit 100
- KV hit rate quick agg:
  SELECT sum(kv_hits) / sum(kv_requests) FROM telemetry WHERE cache_tag IN (list) FACET cache_tag TIMESERIES 1m
- Canary vs baseline comparison:
  latency.p95[canary-v2] / latency.p95[baseline] -> compute ratio and alert if >1.3

Operator checklist for safe rollback (idempotent, brief):
- Notify on-call via Slack channel #ops-rollouts with short template (what, when, why, action).
- Flip rollout flag to previous model variant (or reduce canary to 0%).
- Pause any automated rerouting rules that were part of rollout policy.
- Run quick post-rollback smoke: synthetic probe hitting the same route for 3 minutes and confirm latency and error SLOs.

Open questions / TODOs (short-term work list):
- Implement a small synthetic probe that hits the same cache-tag distribution as production canary traffic. (JIRA: INF-1102)
- Define exact sample rates and retention tiers for canary traces in our tracing backend (cost modeling required). (ASSIGNEE: Marcus)
- Add automated compare panels in the dashboard that compute delta-to-baseline with one-click expand for traces.

Notes to self / operator hints:
- When debugging kv-cache miss storms, check for TTL config rollouts that may have coincided with model rollout. Many incidents are correlated, not causal.
- Look for pattern: high p95 + normal p50 suggests tail latency (often batching or device preemption). High p50 + p95 suggests bulk slowdown at model level.
- Use the trace anchor "batch_size" to detect if a canary is inadvertently being served by smaller batches (runtime config mismatch).

References and links:
- CONFLUENCE-PLAT-5234: rollout telemetry guide
- JIRA-INF-980: previous canary incident postmortem
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412 (adaptive sampling changes)

Appendix: example alert rule (pseudo)
- Alert name: canary-latency-spike
- Query: compare_ratio(latency.p95[canary-v2], latency.p95[baseline], window=10m)
- Trigger: ratio > 1.3 for 5m and canary_rps > 5
- Runbook link: /runbooks/canary-latency-spike

This doc is intentionally concise. Keep it updated with actual query snippets when we standardize our metric names and trace field keys. Footnotes: prioritize operator UX (one-click trace jump) over extra computed metrics that bloat dashboards.

Unresolved: how to surface subtle output-quality regressions quickly without full eval harness integration into telemetry (brainstorm: sample 1% outputs and send to lightweight hallucination classifier).

End.
